headline: REA Gives Agents a Forensic Workbench
lede: REA turns reverse engineering into a structured agent workflow, connecting coding assistants and terminal commands to tools such as Ghidra, Hopper, Binwalk, and JADX. Its reports preserve evidence, limitations, and unknowns, keeping autonomous analysis inspectable rather than magical.

headline: AnyPS5 Rebuilds Console Code for Desktop
lede: AnyPS5 attacks platform boundaries at the executable level, relinking PlayStation 5 binaries for Linux and Windows instead of hiding them behind a conventional emulator. Native library replacements, shader recompilation, and explicit compatibility errors define a hard-edged interoperability experiment.

headline: Agent Skills Turns Process Into Infrastructure
lede: Agent Skills packages specification, planning, testing, review, and shipping into repeatable commands for coding agents. Its momentum reflects a practical demand: make AI-assisted development follow engineering gates instead of improvising from prompt to production.

headline: Diagram Design Makes Technical Graphics Brand-Aware
lede: Diagram Design brings polished HTML and SVG templates into the coding loop, mapping a project’s colors and typography into reusable visual tokens. It also remakes Mermaid and draw.io files into accessible, audience-specific graphics without a Figma detour.

headline: Open Code Review Brings Agents to the Diff
lede: Alibaba’s command-line reviewer combines deterministic file selection with agentic investigation, producing line-level findings across diffs, commits, directories, and full files. JSON output, resumable sessions, configurable rules, and multiple model endpoints make it a practical instrument for the review pipeline.

headline: Knowledge Plugins Turn Claude Into a Team
lede: Anthropic’s file-based plugins give Claude role-specific skills, commands, and connectors for work spanning legal, finance, product, research, and operations. MCP links those specialists to systems such as Jira, Slack, Notion, and data warehouses, turning generic assistance into governed workflow infrastructure.

headline: LiteLLM Routes the Growing Model Maze
lede: LiteLLM normalizes calls to more than 100 model providers behind a shared SDK and gateway, with routing, fallbacks, spend tracking, logging, and guardrails. It gives platform teams one control plane for applications that would otherwise accumulate a tangle of provider-specific integrations.

headline: Agent Skills Draws a Route From Idea to Ship
lede: This collection lays out a staged construction plan for AI-assisted software: discover requirements, write a specification, implement, test, review, and release. Each Markdown skill adds checkpoints and verification steps that let teams adapt the method without surrendering control to an opaque automation layer.

headline: ArtCraft Builds Worlds Before Rendering Them
lede: ArtCraft treats generative media as a scene-building problem, giving creators canvases, cameras, poses, meshes, and compositing tools before they call an image, video, audio, or world model. The desktop IDE turns prompt experiments into repeatable visual iterations across a crowded field of generators.

headline: LingBot-Map Reconstructs Long Streams in Motion
lede: LingBot-Map streams camera poses, dense geometry, and persistent maps from image sequences through a feed-forward 3D foundation model. Its cached attention and geometric memory target roughly 20 frames per second across sequences beyond 10,000 frames, with checkpoints and demos ready for direct evaluation.
